newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: UNION SLAMS EXPENSE OF INTERSTATE CABINET MEETINGS
The Community and Public Sector Union says in an environment of public sector cutbacks, the Prime Minister and Cabinet should be holding more meetings in Canberra to save money.
The Union has hit out at the expense of sending support staff, politicians, and senior bureaucrats interstate to meetings.
The Union's ACT Assistant Branch Secretary Mark Lott says it's an expense the Government can ill afford.
Mr Lott says every time senior bureaucrats travel out of the Capital it creates pressure on the public purse.
He says there's also the actual lost working time to be considered in the time it takes to travel between the meetings.
MARTIN BRYANT'S HOUSE SOLD FOR UNDISCLOSED AMOUNT
In Hobart, the former home of Port Arthur killer, Martin Bryant has been sold.
Selling agent, Graham Hutcheon, says a confidentiality agreement with the purchasers prevents his disclosing the sale price of the New Town property.
Meanwhile, it's been revealed Martin Bryant has tried to commit suicide twice while in Hobart's Risdon Prison.
The Prison hospital's head of nursing says on the first occasion Bryant used bandages to tie around his neck, and more recently he tried to swallow a rolled-up tube of toothpaste.
Mr De Bonford says both times intense security, provided by three cameras in his cell, prevented him succeeding.
TOURISM INDUSTRY WORRIED ABOUT JOBS
The Tourism Task Force is worried about the effects on tourism industry jobs, of a four-year funding reduction plan for the Australian Tourism Commission.
Task Force boss, Christopher Brown, says this follows yesterday's release of the latest unemployment figures showing 811-thousand people in Australia were looking for work.
Mr Brown says the possiblity that the four-year funding reduction plan could be brought forward will further reduce the Commission's ability to advertise Australia overseas meaning fewer jobs.
The Task Force was particularly concerned about the youth unemployment rate of 28 per cent.
EDUCATION MINISTERS MEETING IN MELBOURNE
A strategy to deal with paedophilia in schools will be put to today's meeting of education ministers in Melbourne.
The New South Wales Government is calling for nation-wide mandatory notification of child sexual assault, in all government and private schools.
It also wants a national teachers' licence, based on good character and controlled by an independent register.
The Federal Schools Minister, David Kemp, will use today's meeting to push his plan for national literacy tests for year three pupils.
The issue is expected to be hotly debated - with some states opposing Dr Kemp's threat to withdraw education funding if literacy levels fall below a national benchmark.
HERRON SAYS ABORIGINAL CONTRACT A TASTE OF THINGS TO COME
Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron says white people should wake up to themselves and stop being paternalistic towards indigenous Australians.
This follows the landing of a 15 million dollar transport contract by the Koutha Aboriginal Development Corporation and a transport company.
Senator Herron says there's the potential for many more Aboriginal businessess to get out there and perform, and they should be given the opportunity to do so.
The five year contract to carry copper-gold concentrate from the Ernest Henry Mine to Mount Isa in north western Queensland will provide more jobs for Aboriginal people in the region.
GREENPEACE SHOCKED AT TOXIC CHEMICAL USE IN NT
Greenpeace says the Northern Territory Government is lazy for not banning a toxic pesticide which has been prohibited in the rest of the country since 1995.
Spokesman, Matt Ruckel says the pesticide Chlordane will be available in the Territory for another two years.
Mr Ruckel says all other states have brought into place alternatives to such chemicals, and says he's shocked at the Territory's inability to do the same.
Australian and New Zealand primary industry ministers last week voted to allow the Territory a further two years to phase out the toxic chemical.
